question: Should outbound recipient allowlisting be a shared channel/plugin SDK policy, a Slack-only config field, or an acceptance case under the broader human-chat outbound guardrail work?
rationale: The missing enforcement is clear from source, but adding a public outbound authorization knob sets a security boundary and config/API contract that automation should not choose without maintainer product and security direction.

options.title: Shared outbound policy
options.body: Define a generic outbound recipient allowlist contract, implement Slack first, and leave other channels to adopt the same seam.

options.title: Slack-only field
options.body: Add channels.slack.allowTo or a similar Slack-owned field now, accepting possible later migration into a shared policy.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Track this as a concrete recipient-allowlist acceptance case under #87870 rather than keeping a separate Slack-specific item.

recommendation.title: Shared outbound policy
recommendation.body: Define a generic outbound recipient allowlist contract, implement Slack first, and leave other channels to adopt the same seam.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing signal from previous issue mentions and recent outbound policy/refactor history.
